When creator Vince Gilligan originally pitched and wrote the first season of Breaking Bad, he fully intended for Jesse Pinkman to be a short-lived character. The original plan was for Jesse to be brutally murdered by a rival drug dealer by the ninth episode of the first season, serving primarily as a tragic plot device to push Walter White further into the criminal underworld. However, the 2007–2008 Writers Guild of America strike unexpectedly cut the first season short at only seven episodes, inadvertently saving the character. More importantly, Aaron Paul’s performance and his undeniable, magnetic chemistry with Bryan Cranston were so compelling right out of the gate that Gilligan realized killing off Jesse would be a colossal mistake. Pinkman ultimately survived to become the emotional anchor and moral conscience of the entire series.

Breaking Bad (2008–2013), created by Vince Gilligan, starring Bryan Cranston, Aaron Paul, Anna Gunn, Dean Norris, Giancarlo Esposito. A mild-mannered high school chemistry teacher diagnosed with terminal lung cancer partners with a former student to manufacture and sell crystal meth, rapidly descending into the violent, morally corrupt world of the drug cartel to secure his family’s financial future.
